blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights this 2015 paper as a foundational survey of Bitcoin and cryptocurrency technology, breaking down its core components into transactions and scripts, consensus and mining, and the peer-to-peer network. The blog emphasizes the paper's systematic analysis of Bitcoin's stability and practical workings, noting that while Bitcoin has functioned surprisingly well in practice, research is needed to understand *why* it works and whether it will continue to do so as conditions evolve. Colyer praises the paper's clarity in explaining Bitcoin's ad-hoc scripting language, the Nakamoto consensus mechanism, and the role of miners and transaction fees. He also underscores the paper's discussion of Bitcoin's governance challenges and the five key properties (eventual consensus, exponential convergence, liveness, correctness, and fairness) that underpin its stability.
paper_title: SoK: Research perspectives and challenges for Bitcoin and cryptocurrency
